assessments.reasoning: The 1995 York report entry identifies the authors and report number. Its abstract uses ISETL-LINDA as the name of the parallel language they developed by extending ISETL. This supports a distinct dialect identity within the report’s historical scope.

challenge.method: Could ISETL-LINDA be only a report title or another name for Linda?
challenge.results: The abstract itself assigns the name to the language and separately identifies the York Linda variant as the source of its coordination primitives.

limitations: The proposed dialect represents the dated York authors’ ISETL extension, not other Linda embeddings.
